title: Chuniya, Son of Yosef ben Pachses the Priest
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: The Sifra, Emor (Hyman cites 9), tells of Yosef ben Pachses, who developed a lesion on his leg. The physician wanted to cut it away. Yosef called his son Nechunya and said, “Until now you had a duty to attend to me. From now on, leave, for a priest may not incur ritual impurity for a limb severed from his living father.” The story also appears in Jerusalem Talmud Nazir (Hyman cites 3:1), where the son is called Nechunyah ben Yose.

notes.text: The complete amputation story is in Jerusalem Talmud Nazir7:1, not the supplied3:1. The heading Chuniya and body Nechunya/Nechunyah, and Yosef/Yose in the father’s name, remain distinct supplied forms. The rule concerns whether a priest may incur impurity, not whether an amputated limb can transmit it.

No new whole primary scalar was supplied. The earlier Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 7:1 consultation is inherited beside supplied 3:1; neither the Sifra Emor-9 numbering scheme nor the difference's printed origin is newly established. Heading Chuniya, body Nechunya/Nechunyah, and father Yosef/Yose remain separate supplied forms. נומי denotes the lesion in Hyman's narrative; no precise modern diagnosis is supplied. The rule concerns a priest's permission to incur impurity for a severed limb, not denial that the limb transmits impurity. The son is sent away from attending to his father; no family identity is newly admitted.

The story is at Sifra, Emor, Section 1:14 and Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 7:1:4 in the consulted editions. Both describe a hair’s breadth left attached before the father speaks. The Sifra calls the son both Nechunya and Chuniya and names the father Yosef, while the Jerusalem Talmud reads Nechunyah and Yose. Hyman abridges the story, and his printed locators remain as cited.
